headline: Highest risk is medium data leakage/cascading error: unstructured reads files and runs subprocesses while argo-workflows can pass artifacts/parameters into downstream steps.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but argo-workflows can pass artifacts/parameters and unstructured reads documents/files, so a manual copy or file bridge could carry prompt-like content. The pair lacks evidence of a default instruction-parsing bridge, so this stays low rather than medium.
conditions: IF the operator wires argo-workflows outputs into unstructured document inputs without sanitization, prompt-like content can traverse the pair.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is introduced, injected instructions may be reinterpreted by unstructured.
mitigations: Add a content-sanitization step before handing artifacts from argo-workflows to unstructured.
Use separate directories for workflow outputs and document inputs.
Require explicit human review of any text that will be re-ingested as instructions.
Disable ad hoc copy-paste between the two systems for operational runs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Argo-workflows touches artifacts and parameters, while unstructured reads filesystem documents and processes text/images. In a shared workspace, either agent could expose file contents to the other’s processing path, creating a plausible leakage route in default-style deployments. No stronger isolation is documented here, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or artifact directory, document contents can flow from argo-workflows into unstructured.
IF sensitive artifacts are stored where unstructured can read them, those contents may be processed and surfaced in outputs.
mitigations: Place sensitive artifacts in a separate directory not mounted into unstructured.
Restrict unstructured to a narrow input path per run.
Redact secrets from workflow artifacts before document parsing.
Use per-job ephemeral workspaces with automatic cleanup.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Argo-workflows can orchestrate API-driven jobs, while unstructured can write the filesystem, spawn subprocesses, and install packages. If both are given the same mutable workspace, their write paths can collide even though no locking is documented. The pair therefore has an overlapping-mutation risk, but not enough evidence for high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or artifact store, file clobbering or inconsistent outputs can occur.
IF argo-workflows launches multiple unstructured instances against shared mutable state, race conditions become likely.
mitigations: Assign each run a unique output directory.
Serialize writes to shared artifacts with an external lock.
Mount shared paths read-only except for one designated writer.
Use workflow-level naming conventions to avoid collisions.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Argo-workflows can produce artifacts and parameters that downstream steps consume, and unstructured can transform those inputs into parsed text. If the workflow treats unstructured output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into later steps. The interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF argo-workflows feeds unstructured output directly into a later automated step, any parsing error can propagate.
IF downstream tasks trust unstructured output without validation, incorrect extracted text can drive bad actions.
mitigations: Insert a validation step between parsing and downstream action.
Require schema checks on extracted fields before use.
Flag low-confidence parses for human review.
Keep downstream actions read-only until outputs are verified.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only document generic data classes, so there is no direct evidence of a residency or certification mismatch. The only compliance-relevant concern is that unstructured reads documents while argo-workflows handles artifacts/parameters, which could matter if regulated data is placed in shared storage. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise, but no specific breach is shown.
conditions: IF regulated documents are stored in a shared workspace accessible to unstructured, compliance obligations may be implicated.
IF the operator routes restricted data through workflow artifacts, retention and access controls must be checked.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workflow artifacts.
Document retention settings for both systems before deployment.
Use separate storage buckets for regulated and non-regulated data.
Review privacy policy and data-handling terms before processing sensitive documents.
